items.english: The mother, leaning against the wall, silently bending her head, was serving onto white plates the beef and onions and carrots and potatoes stewed in the deep blue pot. And about to say something, she put a potato, cooked sweet and soft, into her mouth and looked at the man's face, but as if she had noticed something, she suddenly closed her mouth and gazed blankly at a far-off place.

The potato in her mouth was hard and gritty, just as if frozen, and tasted very bad. As if startled, she silently chewed it over again with her front teeth, but before she knew it her heart had bent down, lonely.
notes: I keep the sinking of the heart as a bending down, without making it stand for anything beyond the mouthful.

items.english: She remembered the suffering and sadness and weariness of the days. And the tasteless, unconcerned, cold badness of the potato gave her a quiet, lonely, far-removed heart. She pictured the poor, sadness-filled, real life since her marriage.
notes: "unconcerned" renders a doubtful phrase; the potato's badness feels coldly apart from her, with nothing to do with her.

items.english: And it seemed, too, like a life that had gone on for so very long. She suddenly felt as if she herself had grown quite old. And with a distant heart she quietly remembered the quiet days filled with tears, and the days spent threatened and afraid for material things, and each of the days grieved and suffered through illness. But to her remembering them now, everything was like a dream. Suffering and sadness, too, were like a fond dream.
notes: "fond" is kept deliberately to hold the link to the paired nouns fond remembrance and forgiveness in the vision to come.

items.english: And when she thought about it, it was only some three years of life since their marriage.
Before she knew it, as if her attention had been caught by something, she gazed blankly toward the distance. Before she knew it, her quiet heart was seeing a picture like a phantom.
